title: Deep Filter Controller module hierarchy
purpose: Prevent another 1200+ line implementation surface by splitting controls, renderers, and CSS into domain, subdomain, and block modules.
objective: Make future per-filter polish safe to execute by keeping each authored plugin file in the 200 to 400 line range.
scope_boundary: In scope: StyleControls module extraction, line-budget guard, behavior-preserving renderer extraction, CSS module extraction, and per-filter execution gates. Out of scope: adding new visual features while the monolith still owns the surface.
entry_condition: DEC-EIT-014 is accepted and current plugin source is clean.
exit_condition: StyleControls.php is an orchestrator and future filter work has a bounded module destination.
completion_criteria: A line-budget guard exists and fails oversized authored plugin files.
StyleControls modules are split by shared surface and filter type.
Complex types use subdomain files instead of one large type module.
Existing Elementor control IDs are preserved.
WP-CLI robustness checks still pass after extraction.

phases.title: Guard
phases.purpose: Add file-size budget validation before refactoring.

phases.title: Renderers
phases.purpose: Extract complex widget render branches without markup drift.

phases.title: CSS
phases.purpose: Split frontend/editor CSS by shared surface and filter type.

phases.title: Execution gates
phases.purpose: Queue one implementation task per audited filter type.
phases.evidence: TASK-FC-053 through TASK-FC-062 are queued and gated by completed audits plus TASK-FC-050, TASK-FC-051, and TASK-FC-052.

acceptance_criteria: No authored module crosses 400 lines without a written split rationale.
No new control ID is renamed during behavior-preserving extraction.
No CSS load-order change breaks existing widget output.
stop_conditions: A feature request starts before modularization guardrails exist.
A module exceeds 450 lines during extraction.
Saved Elementor control IDs or rendered selectors are renamed without a migration decision.
